result.paraphrase: GIGABYTE AORUS 2TB M.2 NVMe SSD. Description: 2 TB capacity, M.2 form factor. Features include an M.2 2280 form factor, PCI-Express 4.0 x4 and NVMe 1.3 interface, 2000GB total capacity, sequential read speeds up to 5000 MB/s, sequential write speeds up to 4400 MB/s, Wear Leveling and Over-Provision technologies, TRIM and S.M.A.R.T support, a full-body copper heat spreader, and a limited 5-year warranty. World’s first PCIe 4.0x4 controller: the Phison PS5016-E16, built with 28nm manufacturing technology. This advanced process gives the PS5016-E16 enough compute power for ECC processing when using the latest 3D TLC NAND flash. It also offers eight NAND channels with 32 CE targets, DDR4 DRAM caching, and a PCIe 4.0x4 interface, along with NVMe 1.3, LDPC error correction, Wear Leveling, and Over-Provision technologies to enhance SSD reliability and durability. High-quality NAND flash for performance: TOSHIBA BiCS4 96-layer 3D TLC (800MT/s). Toshiba BiCS4 NAND Flash improves circuitry and architecture by increasing to 96 layers for greater storage density per unit area. The 800MT/s throughput of the AORUS NVMe Gen 4 SSD far exceeds PCIe 3.0x4 devices for better storage performance. Extreme storage performance: with its new PCIe 4.0 controller, the AORUS NVMe Gen 4 SSD reaches blazing speeds of up to 5,000 MB/s sequential read and up to 4,400 MB/s sequential write. Sequential read performance for PCIe 4.0 SSDs is up to 40% faster than PCIe 3.0 SSDs. Designed for faster, smoother gaming, streaming, and graphics-intensive rendering. Full-body copper thermal solution for outstanding PCIe 4.0 SSD performance: the full copper heatsink accounts for heat transfer from key components on both the front and back of the device, including the controller and NAND Flash. Full copper heatsinks provide 69% higher heat transfer capacity than aluminum heatsinks, giving the AORUS NVMe Gen4 SSD excellent dissipation for read/write performance. Efficient copper heat spreader design: compared with a plated M.2 heat spreader, the new efficient copper heat spreaders with 27 fins increase surface area to improve thermal transfer from heat sources and reach thermal balance sooner. The optimized fin-array design also provides strong heat exchange regardless of airflow direction. Together, these designs help the key components of the PCIe 4.0 SSD stay within suitable operating temperature under ultra-high transfer rates.
